- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment cools.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over 3–5 days, model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average before forecasting to reduce noise.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 1–2 days after peak), model should adjust downward by 1–3% per day.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day trend instead of full forecast.
